To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new method to study the high electric field response of dielectrics, and that the method predicts a de-screening of Coulomb interaction due the combined effect of collisional broadening (due to electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions) and the electric field.

(i) The high-field dielectric response of the system is determined by the field-dependent polarization function; (ii) The field-dependent polarization can be expressed in terms of the field-dependent self energy; (iii) The high-field self-energy can be obtained from the solution of the Airy-coordinate Schrödinger equation; (iv) The high-field polarization is obtained from the solution to the Airy-coordinate Keldysh equation.
the Coulomb interaction is screened by the high-frequency dielectric response of the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of high-field transport properties in semiconductor materials, in particular in the regime where electron-impurity scattering is the dominant scattering mechanism.
the development of new theoretical methods for the investigation of the high field dielectric response of solids.
the high-field dielectric response in semiconductors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
de-screening is a general feature of high-field dielectric response.
the high-field response of the dielectric is dominated by the collisional de-screening of Coulomb interaction and not the Stark shift of the single-particle energies.
the Coulomb interaction is screened by the high field, and the screening length is determined by the collisional broadening.
